title: Northern Zhou
capsule: The Northern Zhou (Bei Zhou) was one of the Northern Dynasties of China, ruling from its capital Chang'an over the upper Wei River basin and progressively wider north Chinese territories from 557 to 581. Founded by Yuwen Jue after deposing the Western Wei puppet regime, it reached its territorial apex under Emperor Wu (r. 560–578), who conquered rival Northern Qi in 577 and reunified north China for the first time in over a century. Emperor Wu also suppressed Buddhism, redistributing monastic wealth and clergy to strengthen the agrarian tax base. The dynasty ended in 581 when the regent Yang Jian — founder of the Sui — usurped the throne, beginning the short-lived but transformative Sui reunification of all China.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Northern Zhou's core territory in the Wei River basin is well documented through dynastic histories (Zhou Shu) and archaeological sites; frontier boundaries with Tujue and the Liang in the south are approximate.
